core_claim: Oxford founded its colleges in two short bursts seven centuries apart; the 156-year silence and the dozen defunct colleges hidden in the count are the real story.

edt_01.label: Hook — Guess Oxford's oldest college
edt_01.title: Which is Oxford's oldest college?
edt_01.editorial_notes: The 15-year window (1249/1263/1264) must be exact. Rewley Abbey 1201 is the trap answer — make clear it is not a real college.

edt_02.label: The two waves
edt_02.title: Two waves, seven centuries apart
edt_02.editorial_notes: 9 colleges each in 19th and 20th c.; 1850-1899 window = 9. Keep barbell framing.

edt_03.label: The 156-year silence
edt_03.title: The Georgian silence
edt_03.editorial_notes: 156 years (1714-1870) is the headline number. 18th c. = exactly 1 college (Worcester).

edt_04.label: The Reformation churn
edt_04.title: Destruction dressed as growth
edt_04.editorial_notes: 11 of 50 rows are defunct/merged/non-residential; ~39 survive. Cardinal->Henry VIII's->Christ Church is one institution thrice.

edt_05.label: The Victorians open the gates
edt_05.title: The women's colleges arrive
edt_05.editorial_notes: Elizabeth Wordsworth founded LMH (1878) and St Hugh's (1886). Women could not take degrees until 1920 — keep the 42-year gap.

edt_06.label: Saints become surnames
edt_06.title: From saints to surnames
edt_06.editorial_notes: 17 religious vs 20 personal namesakes of 37. Crests encode founder heraldry — this is where the coat-of-arms gallery belongs.

edt_07.label: The newest college and the limits of the data
edt_07.title: The newest college, and the honest holes
edt_07.editorial_notes: Reuben 2019, first since Kellogg 1990, £80m gift, first students 2021. 49/50 blank mottos; only Magdalen. End on tension, not summary.
